messages.author: 1a3038be6b196f6d
messages.subject: Need help from lavan pakage users (Reverese effect)
parts:
Dear Lavaan users
Need some help in addressing the problem below.

Code shown using lavaan package in R-Studio

BE ~ x1+x2+x3
a ~ x1+x2+x3 + BE + b
b ~ x1+x2+x3 + BE + a

Warning message:
In .local(object, ...) :
  lavaan WARNING: fit measures not available if model did not converge

However, if i remove either one them of 'a' or 'b' then model shows fair results. But i want to check the effect of 'b' on 'a' and 'a' on 'b'
I have also attached image of framework

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Need help from lavan pakage users (Reverese effect)
parts:
You cannot estimate that model. The model is statistically not identified. In order to estimate the reciprocal effects of a on b and b on a, at the least either a or b will need a predictor which is unshared with the other variable (see Rigdon 1995). However, convention would allow for residual covariance between a and b. With free residual covariance, then both a and b will need a predictor not share with the other variable. I am not sure why lavaan has not detected the identification problem.

Rigdon, E. E. (1995). A necessary and sufficient identification rule for structural models estimated in practice. Multivariate behavioral research, 30(3), 359-383.

messages.subject: Re: Need help from lavan pakage users (Reverese effect)
parts: I see that a now has x3 as a predictor while b now has x4 as a predictor. The coefficients for x3 and x4 in these equations must be large. I suggest estimating a model without the reciprocal effects, to make sure that the coefficients are substantial in that case. You might use those estimates as starting values in the reciprocal relations model. Sometimes the iterative estimation process gets stuck in a bad patch of parameter space. If you can provide good starting values (not near 0, and on the correct side of 0), that will sometimes help you to achieve convergence
